# Fingerling (05, engineer) — BAD-015

## Brief
Objective: fix the "Set the profiles_web password" step in .github/workflows/server-deploy.yml so it writes the password with the pooler-url file the Supabase CLI actually produces, and correct the two documents that describe that file.

What happened. PR A (#346) merged and Server deploy run 34926953514 went green (the step never fails the job, by design), but the step wrote nothing and logged: "supabase/.temp/pooler-url does not carry the ':[YOUR-PASSWORD]@' placeholder this step strips. profiles_web's password was NOT written." The role exists on production with no password, so PR B's /status probe would fail; PR B is held until this lands and Server deploy is re-run.

The real format, from a `supabase link` by the same CLI version CI pins (2.114.0), is a URL with no password field at all:
  postgresql://postgres.<project-ref>@aws-0-ca-central-1.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres
(one line, the ref redacted here). No `:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@`, no `%5BYOUR-PASSWORD%5D`, no colon in the userinfo. The step's `url=${raw/:\[YOUR-PASSWORD\]@/@}` therefore leaves the string unchanged and the "unchanged means the placeholder is missing" guard fires. Everything after it would have worked: `PGPASSWORD="$SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD" psql "$url" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v pw="$PROFILES_DB_PASSWORD" -q -c "alter role profiles_web with password :'pw'"`.

The fix, in that step only:
 - Accept the URL as the CLI writes it today (no password field). Still strip a placeholder if one is ever present, in either spelling the Go url package could produce (`:[YOUR-PASSWORD]@` literal, or `:%5BYOUR-PASSWORD%5D@` percent-encoded), and drop the "unchanged" error entirely: an unchanged URL is the normal case now.
 - Keep one sanity check that is actually diagnostic: the file must be a single `postgresql://` URL whose host contains `pooler.supabase.com`; on any other shape, log the URL with the userinfo redacted (never the raw string, in case a CLI version ever embeds the real password) and exit 0 as the step's contract requires.
 - Keep PGPASSWORD for the superuser password and psql's `-v pw` quoting for the new one; never splice either into the URL or the SQL.
 - Update the step's comment so it describes the file's real shape and names the CLI version it was observed on (2.114.0), and keep the step's never-fail contract and its warning/error annotations as they are.
Also correct the two documents that repeat the wrong shape: server/README.md (the PROFILES_DB_PASSWORD paragraphs, if they describe the placeholder) and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-public-profile-pages-design.md § 5 (the `sed "s/\[YOUR-PASSWORD\]/…"` snippet and the sentence after it). Say the file carries no password and the step supplies both passwords out of band. If test/server/schema.test.mjs or any other test pins the step's text, update the pin to the new text.

Proof (quote the decisive lines in `member result`):
 - `actionlint .github/workflows/server-deploy.yml` (at /opt/homebrew/bin/actionlint): exit 0.
 - A local dry run of the step's shell body: copy the `run:` script to a scratch file, point it at a scratch directory holding a `supabase/.temp/pooler-url` with exactly the real format above (use a fake ref), put a stub `psql` first on PATH that prints its arguments and `PGPASSWORD` (masked to its length) and exits 0, set the three variables to dummy values, and run it: show that it reaches psql with the unchanged URL, `-v pw=<dummy>` and `-c "alter role profiles_web with password :'pw'"`, and prints "profiles_web's password is set". Repeat with a file carrying each placeholder spelling to show both are stripped, with a malformed file to show the redacted diagnostic and exit 0, and with PROFILES_DB_PASSWORD empty to show the existing warning path. Never run the real step, never touch production, never `supabase login`.
 - `npm test` if a test pin changed; say which suite.
Deliverables: .github/workflows/server-deploy.yml, server/README.md, docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-public-profile-pages-design.md, test/server/**.
